``` - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech finishes - Automatic: Screen readers announce counter updates without manual focus management --- ## Pipeline Visualization (VIZ-01) ### Stage Display **Requirements:** - Show all 5 stages: IF (Instruction Fetch), ID (Instruction Decode), EX (Execute), MEM (Memory), WB (Write Back) - Display current instruction in each stage - Indicate active stages (instruction present vs. empty/bubble) **Implementation approach:** **Stage card structure:** ```html
IF Instruction Fetch
NOP
``` **Color-coded stages (research finding):** Educational CPU visualizers use distinct colors per stage to help students track instruction flow through pipeline. | Stage | Color | Rationale | |-------|-------|-----------| | IF | Green (#4CAF50) | Start of pipeline (green = go) | | ID | Blue (#2196F3) | Decoding/analysis phase | | EX | Orange (#FF9800) | Active computation (warm color = activity) | | MEM | Purple (#9C27B0) | Memory access (distinct from computation) | | WB | Red (#F44336) | Write back (red = completion) | **CSS implementation:** ```css .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="ID"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-id-color); } /* etc. */ ``` **Active stage indicator:** - Add `.active` class when instruction present - Remove when stage holds bubble (NOP/stall) - CSS: Brighter border, slight shadow ### Instruction Display **Format:** Assembly mnemonic + operands (e.g., `ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`) **Empty stage display:** `NOP` (no operation) or `[empty]` (TBD: prefer NOP to match assembly syntax) **CPUState metadata usage:** ```javascript state.pipeline.stages.forEach(stage => { const card = this.container.querySelector(`[data-stage="${stage.name}"]`); const instructionEl = card.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); instructionEl.textContent = stage.instruction?.mnemonic || 'NOP'; card.classList.toggle('active', stage.instruction !== null); }); ``` --- ## Register Visualization (VIZ-02, VIZ-03) ### Register Grid Layout **Requirements:** - Display all 32 registers ($0-$31) - Show current value for each register - Highlight registers that changed in current cycle (VIZ-03) **Grid structure:** ```html
$0 0x00000000
``` **CSS Grid layout:** ```css .register-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } ``` - Responsive: Adjusts columns to viewport width - Consistent sizing: `minmax(120px, 1fr)` ensures readable cells ### Value Display Format **Hex by default:** `0x00000000` (8 hex digits, zero-padded) **Justification:** - Educational standard: Academic CPU simulators use hex (matches memory dumps, opcodes) - Concise: 8 characters vs. 10 for decimal - Deferred toggle: Phase 11+ can add hex/decimal/binary switcher **Register $0 special case:** - Always displays `0x00000000` (hardwired to zero in RISC architectures) - Grayed out styling to indicate read-only ### Change Highlighting (VIZ-03) **CPUState metadata (from Phase 9):** ```javascript state.changedRegisters = [5, 7]; // Registers $5 and $7 changed this cycle ``` **Selective DOM update strategy:** ```javascript // GOOD: Only update changed registers (1-3 per cycle typically) state.changedRegisters.forEach(regIndex => { const cell = this.container.querySelector(`[data-register="${regIndex}"]`); const valueEl = cell.querySelector('.register-value'); valueEl.textContent = formatHex(state.registers[regIndex]); cell.classList.add('changed'); }); // BAD: Full re-render (32 register updates per frame) state.registers.forEach((value, index) => { /* update all */ }); ``` **CSS transition:** ```css .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } ``` - Yellow highlight fades out over 300ms - Remove `.changed` class after transition completes **Performance consideration:** - Non-pipelined simulation (Phase 9): ~1-3 registers change per cycle - Pipelined simulation (Phase 12+): Up to 5 registers per cycle (one per stage) - Selective updates prevent DOM thrashing (3 updates vs. 32) ### Typography **Monospace font (research finding):** Monospace fonts critical for register values (alignment, readability). **Font stack:** ```css .register-value, .instruction-text { font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } ``` **Justification:** - Monaco/Consolas: System monospace fonts (macOS/Windows) - Courier New: Fallback (universal) - No external fonts: Keep performance optimal (no font loading delay) --- ## Execution State (VIZ-06) ### Counter Display **Requirements:** - Display cycle count (increments each animation frame) - Display instruction count (increments when instruction completes WB stage) **Implementation:** ```html

Cycle: 0

Instructions: 0

``` **Update logic:** ```javascript render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } ``` **CPUState fields (from Phase 9):** - `state.cycleCount`: Total cycles elapsed (increments every frame) - `state.instructionCount`: Total instructions completed (increments when instruction exits WB stage) ### Accessibility (aria-live) **Screen reader behavior:** - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech completes - Example: "Cycle: 5, Instructions: 2" (spoken when counters update) **Announcement frequency:** - Non-pipelined (Phase 9): Every cycle (slow pace: 2 FPS base) - Pipelined (Phase 12+): Every cycle (may need throttling if too frequent) **Future enhancement (Phase 11+):** - Add `aria-atomic="true"` to announce full region content (both counters together) - Add `aria-relevant="text"` to only announce text changes (not additions/removals) --- ## Styling Strategy ### CSS Architecture **File structure:** ``` cpu-visualizer/ styles/ visualization.css # Phase 10: Layout, components, colors design-system.css # Existing: Shared tokens (already in codebase) ``` **CSS custom properties (design tokens):** ```css :root { /* Existing tokens from design-system.css */ --color-primary: #2E7D32; /* Forest green */ --color-background: #FFFFFF; --color-text: #212121; /* New tokens for Phase 10 */ --stage-if-color: #4CAF50; /* Green */ --stage-id-color: #2196F3; /* Blue */ --stage-ex-color: #FF9800; /* Orange */ --stage-mem-color: #9C27B0; /* Purple */ --stage-wb-color: #F44336; /* Red */ --color-highlight-yellow: #FFF9C4; /* Register change highlight */ } ``` **Advantages:** - Centralized: All colors defined in one place - Themeable: Future dark mode support (override custom properties) - Consistent: Matches existing design system ### Component-Specific Styles **Pipeline stage cards:** ```css .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); /* Color-coded */ border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; /* Thicker border when active */ } ``` **Register cells:** ```css .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); } .register-cell[data-register="0"] { opacity: 0.6; /* Register $0 always zero, visual cue */ } ``` **Execution counters:** ```css [data-execution-view] p { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0; } [data-execution-view] span { font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; } ``` --- ## Performance Considerations ### Selective DOM Updates **Problem:** Updating all 32 registers every frame causes layout thrashing (browser recalculates styles 32 times). **Solution:** CPUState tracks `changedRegisters` array, only update those elements. **Performance impact:** - Full update: 32 DOM writes + 32 style recalculations per frame - Selective update: 1-3 DOM writes + 1-3 style recalculations per frame - **~10x faster** for typical case (1-3 changed registers) ### Batch DOM Writes **Use DocumentFragment for initial render:** ```javascript const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Register Display Format **Question:** Hex only, or hex + decimal toggle? **Recommendation:** Hex only for Phase 10 (simplicity), defer toggle to Phase 11 (interactive controls). **Justification:** - Hex is educational standard (matches academic tools) - Phase 10 scope: "Basic Visualization" (display works, not UX enhancements) - Phase 11 already adds interactive controls (step/play/pause), natural place for format toggle ### 2. Pipeline Stage Detail Level **Question:** Show full instruction fields (opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) or just mnemonic? **Recommendation:** Mnemonic only for Phase 10 (`ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`), field breakdown in Phase 11. **Justification:** - Phase 10 requirement (VIZ-01): "Display current instruction in each stage" (not field breakdown) - Phase 11 requirement (VIZ-05): "Instruction display shows current instruction with field breakdown" - Keep Phase 10 focused: Layout + rendering, Phase 11 adds detail ### 3. Pipeline Stage Empty State **Question:** Display `NOP` or `[empty]` for empty stages? **Recommendation:** `NOP` (no operation) to match assembly syntax. **Justification:** - Consistent with assembly language conventions - Educational: NOP is a real instruction (students may encounter in code) - Technical: Bubbles in pipeline effectively NOPs (do nothing, advance clock) ### 4. Color Palette Conflict **Question:** Stage colors (green, blue, orange, purple, red) vs. design system primary green (#2E7D32)? **Recommendation:** Use distinct stage colors (from research), keep primary green for UI chrome (header, buttons). **Justification:** - Educational benefit: Color-coded stages help students track instruction flow (established pattern) - Visual hierarchy: Stage colors = content, primary green = navigation/controls - No conflict: Stages use pastel/medium tones (e.g., #4CAF50), primary uses dark tone (#2E7D32) ### 5. Performance Threshold **Question:** How many register updates before performance degrades? **Recommendation:** Measure during implementation (throttle to 3GHz CPU, test with 10+ register changes/frame). **Expected outcome:** - Selective updates (3-5 registers): No performance impact (CSS transitions GPU-accelerated) - Full updates (32 registers): Possible jank at 30+ FPS (forces layout recalculation) - Mitigation: CPUState.changedRegisters prevents full updates by design --- ## Dependencies & Integration ### Phase 9 Outputs (Already Complete) **Required from Phase 9:** 1. **CPUState structure** (cpu-state.js): - `state.pipeline.stages` (array of 5 stages with instruction data) - `state.registers` (Uint32Array of 32 register values) - `state.changedRegisters` (array of register indices that changed) - `state.cycleCount`, `state.instructionCount` 2. **AnimationEngine events** (animation-engine.js): - `cpu:framechange` CustomEvent with `{ state, frameIndex, totalFrames }` payload - Already implemented (09-02-PLAN.md) 3. **Instruction structure** (instruction-set.js): - `instruction.mnemonic` (string, e.g., "ADD") - `instruction.operands` (array, e.g., ["$t0", "$t1", "$t2"]) **Validation:** Existing Phase 9 tests must pass (cpu-state.test.js, animation-engine.test.js). ### Phase 11 Inputs (To Be Consumed) **Outputs from Phase 10:** 1. **Visualization components** (pipeline-view.js, register-view.js, execution-view.js): - Exported classes with `.render(state)` method - Event-driven: Listen to `cpu:framechange`, update DOM 2. **CPUVisualizer coordinator** (cpu-visualizer.js): - Single entry point: `new CPUVisualizer(containerEl)` - Manages child components, delegates rendering 3. **Styling** (visualization.css): - CSS Grid layout (responsive two-column) - Color-coded pipeline stages - Register highlighting transitions **Phase 11 will add:** - Step controls (forward, backward, reset, jump) - Play/pause controls with speed adjustment - Program selector (switch between examples) - Memory visualization (data memory addresses + values) - Instruction detail panel (field breakdown: opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) --- ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Tests **Components to test:** 1. `PipelineView.render(state)` - Stage cards update correctly 2. `RegisterView.render(state)` - Register values update, highlighting works 3. `ExecutionView.render(state)` - Counters increment correctly **Test approach:** - Mock CPUState objects (valid structure, different values) - Dispatch synthetic `cpu:framechange` events - Assert DOM contains expected values, classes **Example test:** ```javascript test('RegisterView highlights changed registers', () => { const state = { registers: new Uint32Array(32), changedRegisters: [5, 7] }; state.registers[5] = 0x12345678; state.registers[7] = 0xABCDEF00; const view = new RegisterView(containerEl); view.render(state); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="5"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="7"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="0"]')).not.toHaveClass('changed'); }); ``` ### Integration Tests **Scenario:** AnimationEngine → CPUVisualizer → DOM updates **Test flow:** 1. Initialize AnimationEngine with pre-scripted sequence (from Phase 9) 2. Initialize CPUVisualizer with container element 3. Call `animationEngine.stepForward()` 4. Assert DOM reflects new state (pipeline stages, registers, counters) **Example test:** ```javascript test('Full animation frame updates visualization', async () => { const sequence = await generateBasicInstructionsSequence(); // Phase 9 function const engine = new AnimationEngine(sequence); const visualizer = new CPUVisualizer(containerEl); engine.stepForward(); // Check pipeline updated const ifStage = containerEl.querySelector('[data-stage="IF"]'); expect(ifStage.textContent).toContain('ADD'); // Check counters updated expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-cycle-count]').textContent).toBe('1'); }); ``` ### Manual Testing **Checklist:** - [ ] All 5 pipeline stages visible on page load - [ ] Registers display in grid layout (4-8 columns depending on viewport) - [ ] Cycle/instruction counters start at 0 - [ ] Step forward → pipeline stages update with instructions - [ ] Step forward → changed registers highlight in yellow - [ ] Highlight fades out after ~300ms - [ ] Counters increment correctly (cycle every step, instruction when WB stage completes) - [ ] Screen reader announces counter changes (test with VoiceOver/NVDA) - [ ] Responsive: Layout adapts to narrow viewport (single column) --- ## Code Examples ### 1. CPUVisualizer (Coordinator) ```javascript // cpu-visualizer.js import { PipelineView } from './pipeline-view.js'; import { RegisterView } from './register-view.js'; import { ExecutionView } from './execution-view.js'; export class CPUVisualizer { constructor(container) { this.container = container; // Initialize child components this.pipelineView = new PipelineView( container.querySelector('[data-pipeline-view]') ); this.registerView = new RegisterView( container.querySelector('[data-register-view]') ); this.executionView = new ExecutionView( container.querySelector('[data-execution-view]') ); // Listen to animation events this.handleFrameChange = this.handleFrameChange.bind(this); window.addEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } handleFrameChange(event) { const { state } = event.detail; // Delegate to child components this.pipelineView.render(state); this.registerView.render(state); this.executionView.render(state); } destroy() { window.removeEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } } ``` ### 2. PipelineView (Stage Visualization) ```javascript // pipeline-view.js export class PipelineView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.stageElements = new Map(); this.initializeStages(); } initializeStages() { const stages = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB']; const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); stages.forEach(stageName => { const stageCard = document.createElement('div'); stageCard.className = 'pipeline-stage'; stageCard.dataset.stage = stageName; stageCard.innerHTML = `
${stageName} ${this.getFullStageName(stageName)}
NOP
`; this.stageElements.set(stageName, stageCard); fragment.appendChild(stageCard); }); this.container.appendChild(fragment); } getFullStageName(abbrev) { const names = { IF: 'Instruction Fetch', ID: 'Instruction Decode', EX: 'Execute', MEM: 'Memory Access', WB: 'Write Back' }; return names[abbrev]; } render(state) { state.pipeline.stages.forEach((stageData, index) => { const stageName = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB'][index]; const stageCard = this.stageElements.get(stageName); const instructionEl = stageCard.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); if (stageData.instruction) { const { mnemonic, operands } = stageData.instruction; instructionEl.textContent = `${mnemonic} ${operands.join(', ')}`; stageCard.classList.add('active'); } else { instructionEl.textContent = 'NOP'; stageCard.classList.remove('active'); } }); } } ``` ### 3. for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Stage cards update correctly 2. `RegisterView.render(state)` - Register values update, highlighting works 3. `ExecutionView.render(state)` - Counters increment correctly **Test approach:** - Mock CPUState objects (valid structure, different values) - IF Instruction Fetch

``` **Color-coded stages (research finding):** Educational CPU visualizers use distinct colors per stage to help students track instruction flow through pipeline. | Stage | Color | Rationale | |-------|-------|-----------| | IF | Green (#4CAF50) | Start of pipeline (green = go) | | ID | Blue (#2196F3) | Decoding/analysis phase | | EX | Orange (#FF9800) | Active computation (warm color = activity) | | MEM | Purple (#9C27B0) | Memory access (distinct from computation) | | WB | Red (#F44336) | Write back (red = completion) | **CSS implementation:** ```css .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="ID"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-id-color); } /* etc. */ ``` **Active stage indicator:** - Add `.active` class when instruction present - Remove when stage holds bubble (NOP/stall) - CSS: Brighter border, slight shadow ### Instruction Display **Format:** Assembly mnemonic + operands (e.g., `ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`) **Empty stage display:** `NOP` (no operation) or `[empty]` (TBD: prefer NOP to match assembly syntax) **CPUState metadata usage:** ```javascript state.pipeline.stages.forEach(stage => { const card = this.container.querySelector(`[data-stage="${stage.name}"]`); const instructionEl = card.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); instructionEl.textContent = stage.instruction?.mnemonic || 'NOP'; card.classList.toggle('active', stage.instruction !== null); }); ``` --- ## Register Visualization (VIZ-02, VIZ-03) ### Register Grid Layout **Requirements:** - Display all 32 registers ($0-$31) - Show current value for each register - Highlight registers that changed in current cycle (VIZ-03) **Grid structure:** ```html
$0 0x00000000
``` **CSS Grid layout:** ```css .register-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } ``` - Responsive: Adjusts columns to viewport width - Consistent sizing: `minmax(120px, 1fr)` ensures readable cells ### Value Display Format **Hex by default:** `0x00000000` (8 hex digits, zero-padded) **Justification:** - Educational standard: Academic CPU simulators use hex (matches memory dumps, opcodes) - Concise: 8 characters vs. 10 for decimal - Deferred toggle: Phase 11+ can add hex/decimal/binary switcher **Register $0 special case:** - Always displays `0x00000000` (hardwired to zero in RISC architectures) - Grayed out styling to indicate read-only ### Change Highlighting (VIZ-03) **CPUState metadata (from Phase 9):** ```javascript state.changedRegisters = [5, 7]; // Registers $5 and $7 changed this cycle ``` **Selective DOM update strategy:** ```javascript // GOOD: Only update changed registers (1-3 per cycle typically) state.changedRegisters.forEach(regIndex => { const cell = this.container.querySelector(`[data-register="${regIndex}"]`); const valueEl = cell.querySelector('.register-value'); valueEl.textContent = formatHex(state.registers[regIndex]); cell.classList.add('changed'); }); // BAD: Full re-render (32 register updates per frame) state.registers.forEach((value, index) => { /* update all */ }); ``` **CSS transition:** ```css .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } ``` - Yellow highlight fades out over 300ms - Remove `.changed` class after transition completes **Performance consideration:** - Non-pipelined simulation (Phase 9): ~1-3 registers change per cycle - Pipelined simulation (Phase 12+): Up to 5 registers per cycle (one per stage) - Selective updates prevent DOM thrashing (3 updates vs. 32) ### Typography **Monospace font (research finding):** Monospace fonts critical for register values (alignment, readability). **Font stack:** ```css .register-value, .instruction-text { font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } ``` **Justification:** - Monaco/Consolas: System monospace fonts (macOS/Windows) - Courier New: Fallback (universal) - No external fonts: Keep performance optimal (no font loading delay) --- ## Execution State (VIZ-06) ### Counter Display **Requirements:** - Display cycle count (increments each animation frame) - Display instruction count (increments when instruction completes WB stage) **Implementation:** ```html

Cycle: 0

Instructions: 0

``` **Update logic:** ```javascript render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } ``` **CPUState fields (from Phase 9):** - `state.cycleCount`: Total cycles elapsed (increments every frame) - `state.instructionCount`: Total instructions completed (increments when instruction exits WB stage) ### Accessibility (aria-live) **Screen reader behavior:** - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech completes - Example: "Cycle: 5, Instructions: 2" (spoken when counters update) **Announcement frequency:** - Non-pipelined (Phase 9): Every cycle (slow pace: 2 FPS base) - Pipelined (Phase 12+): Every cycle (may need throttling if too frequent) **Future enhancement (Phase 11+):** - Add `aria-atomic="true"` to announce full region content (both counters together) - Add `aria-relevant="text"` to only announce text changes (not additions/removals) --- ## Styling Strategy ### CSS Architecture **File structure:** ``` cpu-visualizer/ styles/ visualization.css # Phase 10: Layout, components, colors design-system.css # Existing: Shared tokens (already in codebase) ``` **CSS custom properties (design tokens):** ```css :root { /* Existing tokens from design-system.css */ --color-primary: #2E7D32; /* Forest green */ --color-background: #FFFFFF; --color-text: #212121; /* New tokens for Phase 10 */ --stage-if-color: #4CAF50; /* Green */ --stage-id-color: #2196F3; /* Blue */ --stage-ex-color: #FF9800; /* Orange */ --stage-mem-color: #9C27B0; /* Purple */ --stage-wb-color: #F44336; /* Red */ --color-highlight-yellow: #FFF9C4; /* Register change highlight */ } ``` **Advantages:** - Centralized: All colors defined in one place - Themeable: Future dark mode support (override custom properties) - Consistent: Matches existing design system ### Component-Specific Styles **Pipeline stage cards:** ```css .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); /* Color-coded */ border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; /* Thicker border when active */ } ``` **Register cells:** ```css .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); } .register-cell[data-register="0"] { opacity: 0.6; /* Register $0 always zero, visual cue */ } ``` **Execution counters:** ```css [data-execution-view] p { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0; } [data-execution-view] span { font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; } ``` --- ## Performance Considerations ### Selective DOM Updates **Problem:** Updating all 32 registers every frame causes layout thrashing (browser recalculates styles 32 times). **Solution:** CPUState tracks `changedRegisters` array, only update those elements. **Performance impact:** - Full update: 32 DOM writes + 32 style recalculations per frame - Selective update: 1-3 DOM writes + 1-3 style recalculations per frame - **~10x faster** for typical case (1-3 changed registers) ### Batch DOM Writes **Use DocumentFragment for initial render:** ```javascript const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Register Display Format **Question:** Hex only, or hex + decimal toggle? **Recommendation:** Hex only for Phase 10 (simplicity), defer toggle to Phase 11 (interactive controls). **Justification:** - Hex is educational standard (matches academic tools) - Phase 10 scope: "Basic Visualization" (display works, not UX enhancements) - Phase 11 already adds interactive controls (step/play/pause), natural place for format toggle ### 2. Pipeline Stage Detail Level **Question:** Show full instruction fields (opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) or just mnemonic? **Recommendation:** Mnemonic only for Phase 10 (`ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`), field breakdown in Phase 11. **Justification:** - Phase 10 requirement (VIZ-01): "Display current instruction in each stage" (not field breakdown) - Phase 11 requirement (VIZ-05): "Instruction display shows current instruction with field breakdown" - Keep Phase 10 focused: Layout + rendering, Phase 11 adds detail ### 3. Pipeline Stage Empty State **Question:** Display `NOP` or `[empty]` for empty stages? **Recommendation:** `NOP` (no operation) to match assembly syntax. **Justification:** - Consistent with assembly language conventions - Educational: NOP is a real instruction (students may encounter in code) - Technical: Bubbles in pipeline effectively NOPs (do nothing, advance clock) ### 4. Color Palette Conflict **Question:** Stage colors (green, blue, orange, purple, red) vs. design system primary green (#2E7D32)? **Recommendation:** Use distinct stage colors (from research), keep primary green for UI chrome (header, buttons). **Justification:** - Educational benefit: Color-coded stages help students track instruction flow (established pattern) - Visual hierarchy: Stage colors = content, primary green = navigation/controls - No conflict: Stages use pastel/medium tones (e.g., #4CAF50), primary uses dark tone (#2E7D32) ### 5. Performance Threshold **Question:** How many register updates before performance degrades? **Recommendation:** Measure during implementation (throttle to 3GHz CPU, test with 10+ register changes/frame). **Expected outcome:** - Selective updates (3-5 registers): No performance impact (CSS transitions GPU-accelerated) - Full updates (32 registers): Possible jank at 30+ FPS (forces layout recalculation) - Mitigation: CPUState.changedRegisters prevents full updates by design --- ## Dependencies & Integration ### Phase 9 Outputs (Already Complete) **Required from Phase 9:** 1. **CPUState structure** (cpu-state.js): - `state.pipeline.stages` (array of 5 stages with instruction data) - `state.registers` (Uint32Array of 32 register values) - `state.changedRegisters` (array of register indices that changed) - `state.cycleCount`, `state.instructionCount` 2. **AnimationEngine events** (animation-engine.js): - `cpu:framechange` CustomEvent with `{ state, frameIndex, totalFrames }` payload - Already implemented (09-02-PLAN.md) 3. **Instruction structure** (instruction-set.js): - `instruction.mnemonic` (string, e.g., "ADD") - `instruction.operands` (array, e.g., ["$t0", "$t1", "$t2"]) **Validation:** Existing Phase 9 tests must pass (cpu-state.test.js, animation-engine.test.js). ### Phase 11 Inputs (To Be Consumed) **Outputs from Phase 10:** 1. **Visualization components** (pipeline-view.js, register-view.js, execution-view.js): - Exported classes with `.render(state)` method - Event-driven: Listen to `cpu:framechange`, update DOM 2. **CPUVisualizer coordinator** (cpu-visualizer.js): - Single entry point: `new CPUVisualizer(containerEl)` - Manages child components, delegates rendering 3. **Styling** (visualization.css): - CSS Grid layout (responsive two-column) - Color-coded pipeline stages - Register highlighting transitions **Phase 11 will add:** - Step controls (forward, backward, reset, jump) - Play/pause controls with speed adjustment - Program selector (switch between examples) - Memory visualization (data memory addresses + values) - Instruction detail panel (field breakdown: opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) --- ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Tests **Components to test:** 1. `PipelineView.render(state)` - Stage cards update correctly 2. `RegisterView.render(state)` - Register values update, highlighting works 3. `ExecutionView.render(state)` - Counters increment correctly **Test approach:** - Mock CPUState objects (valid structure, different values) - Dispatch synthetic `cpu:framechange` events - Assert DOM contains expected values, classes **Example test:** ```javascript test('RegisterView highlights changed registers', () => { const state = { registers: new Uint32Array(32), changedRegisters: [5, 7] }; state.registers[5] = 0x12345678; state.registers[7] = 0xABCDEF00; const view = new RegisterView(containerEl); view.render(state); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="5"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="7"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="0"]')).not.toHaveClass('changed'); }); ``` ### Integration Tests **Scenario:** AnimationEngine → CPUVisualizer → DOM updates **Test flow:** 1. Initialize AnimationEngine with pre-scripted sequence (from Phase 9) 2. Initialize CPUVisualizer with container element 3. Call `animationEngine.stepForward()` 4. Assert DOM reflects new state (pipeline stages, registers, counters) **Example test:** ```javascript test('Full animation frame updates visualization', async () => { const sequence = await generateBasicInstructionsSequence(); // Phase 9 function const engine = new AnimationEngine(sequence); const visualizer = new CPUVisualizer(containerEl); engine.stepForward(); // Check pipeline updated const ifStage = containerEl.querySelector('[data-stage="IF"]'); expect(ifStage.textContent).toContain('ADD'); // Check counters updated expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-cycle-count]').textContent).toBe('1'); }); ``` ### Manual Testing **Checklist:** - [ ] All 5 pipeline stages visible on page load - [ ] Registers display in grid layout (4-8 columns depending on viewport) - [ ] Cycle/instruction counters start at 0 - [ ] Step forward → pipeline stages update with instructions - [ ] Step forward → changed registers highlight in yellow - [ ] Highlight fades out after ~300ms - [ ] Counters increment correctly (cycle every step, instruction when WB stage completes) - [ ] Screen reader announces counter changes (test with VoiceOver/NVDA) - [ ] Responsive: Layout adapts to narrow viewport (single column) --- ## Code Examples ### 1. CPUVisualizer (Coordinator) ```javascript // cpu-visualizer.js import { PipelineView } from './pipeline-view.js'; import { RegisterView } from './register-view.js'; import { ExecutionView } from './execution-view.js'; export class CPUVisualizer { constructor(container) { this.container = container; // Initialize child components this.pipelineView = new PipelineView( container.querySelector('[data-pipeline-view]') ); this.registerView = new RegisterView( container.querySelector('[data-register-view]') ); this.executionView = new ExecutionView( container.querySelector('[data-execution-view]') ); // Listen to animation events this.handleFrameChange = this.handleFrameChange.bind(this); window.addEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } handleFrameChange(event) { const { state } = event.detail; // Delegate to child components this.pipelineView.render(state); this.registerView.render(state); this.executionView.render(state); } destroy() { window.removeEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } } ``` ### 2. PipelineView (Stage Visualization) ```javascript // pipeline-view.js export class PipelineView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.stageElements = new Map(); this.initializeStages(); } initializeStages() { const stages = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB']; const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); stages.forEach(stageName => { const stageCard = document.createElement('div'); stageCard.className = 'pipeline-stage'; stageCard.dataset.stage = stageName; stageCard.innerHTML = `
${stageName} ${this.getFullStageName(stageName)}
NOP
`; this.stageElements.set(stageName, stageCard); fragment.appendChild(stageCard); }); this.container.appendChild(fragment); } getFullStageName(abbrev) { const names = { IF: 'Instruction Fetch', ID: 'Instruction Decode', EX: 'Execute', MEM: 'Memory Access', WB: 'Write Back' }; return names[abbrev]; } render(state) { state.pipeline.stages.forEach((stageData, index) => { const stageName = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB'][index]; const stageCard = this.stageElements.get(stageName); const instructionEl = stageCard.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); if (stageData.instruction) { const { mnemonic, operands } = stageData.instruction; instructionEl.textContent = `${mnemonic} ${operands.join(', ')}`; stageCard.classList.add('active'); } else { instructionEl.textContent = 'NOP'; stageCard.classList.remove('active'); } }); } } ``` ### 3. RegisterView (Register Visualization) ```javascript // register-view.js export class RegisterView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.registerCells = []; this.initializeRegisters(); } initializeRegisters() { const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = document.createElement('div'); cell.className = 'register-cell'; cell.dataset.register = i; cell.innerHTML = ` $${i} 0x00000000 `; this.registerCells.push(cell); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); } render(state) { // Selective update: Only changed registers state.changedRegisters.forEach(regIndex => { const cell = this.registerCells[regIndex]; const valueEl = cell.querySelector('.register-value'); // Update value valueEl.textContent = this.formatHex(state.registers[regIndex]); // Add highlight class cell.classList.add('changed'); // Remove after transition setTimeout(() => cell.classList.remove('changed'), 300); }); } formatHex(value) { return '0x' + value.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(8, '0'); } } ``` ### 4. ExecutionView (Counter Display) ```javascript // execution-view.js export class ExecutionView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.cycleEl = container.querySelector('[data-cycle-count]'); this.instructionEl = container.querySelector('[data-instruction-count]'); } render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } } ``` ### 5. CSS (visualization.css) ```css /* Layout */ .cpu-visualizer { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 400px; /* Main + sidebar */ gap: 24px; padding: 24px; } @media (max-width: 768px) { .cpu-visualizer { grid-template-columns: 1fr; /* Stack on mobile */ } } /* Pipeline Stages */ .pipeline-stages { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; } .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left-color: var(--stage-if-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="ID"] { border-left-color: var(--stage-id-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="EX"] { border-left-color: var(--stage-ex-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="MEM"] { border-left-color: var(--stage-mem-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="WB"] { border-left-color: var(--stage-wb-color); } .stage-header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 8px; } .stage-label { font-weight: bold; font-size: 14px; } .stage-name { font-size: 12px; color: #757575; } .instruction-text { font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; font-size: 13px; color: var(--color-text); } /* Register Grid */ .register-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; } .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); } .register-cell[data-register="0"] { opacity: 0.6; /* Register $0 always zero */ } .register-label { font-weight: bold; font-size: 12px; } .register-value { font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } /* Execution State */ [data-execution-view] { margin-top: 24px; } [data-execution-view] p { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0; } [data-execution-view] span { font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; } ``` --- ## Sources 1. font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } ``` **Justification:** - Monaco/Consolas: System monospace fonts (macOS/Windows) - Courier New: Fallback (universal) - No external fonts: Keep performance optimal (no font loading delay) --- ## Execution State (VIZ-06) ### Counter Display **Requirements:** - Display cycle count (increments each animation frame) - Display instruction count (increments when instruction completes WB stage) **Implementation:** ```html

Cycle: 0

Instructions: 0

``` **Update logic:** ```javascript render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } ``` **CPUState fields (from Phase 9):** - `state.cycleCount`: Total cycles elapsed (increments every frame) - `state.instructionCount`: Total instructions completed (increments when instruction exits WB stage) ### Accessibility (aria-live) **Screen reader behavior:** - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech completes - Example: "Cycle: 5, Instructions: 2" (spoken when counters update) **Announcement frequency:** - Non-pipelined (Phase 9): Every cycle (slow pace: 2 FPS base) - Pipelined (Phase 12+): Every cycle (may need throttling if too frequent) **Future enhancement (Phase 11+):** - Add `aria-atomic="true"` to announce full region content (both counters together) - Add `aria-relevant="text"` to only announce text changes (not additions/removals) --- ## Styling Strategy ### CSS Architecture **File structure:** ``` cpu-visualizer/ styles/ visualization.css # Phase 10: Layout, components, colors design-system.css # Existing: Shared tokens (already in codebase) ``` **CSS custom properties (design tokens):** ```css :root { /* Existing tokens from design-system.css */ --color-primary: #2E7D32; /* Orange */ --stage-mem-color: #9C27B0; /* Purple */ --stage-wb-color: #F44336; /* Red */ --color-highlight-yellow: #FFF9C4; /* Register change highlight */ } ``` **Advantages:** - Centralized: All colors defined in one place - Themeable: Future dark mode support (override custom properties) - Consistent: Matches existing design system ### Component-Specific Styles **Pipeline stage cards:** ```css .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left-width: 6px; /* Thicker border when active */ } ``` **Register cells:** ```css .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); Register Display Format **Question:** Hex only, or hex + decimal toggle? **Recommendation:** Hex only for Phase 10 (simplicity), defer toggle to Phase 11 (interactive controls). **Justification:** - Hex is educational standard (matches academic tools) - Phase 10 scope: "Basic Visualization" (display works, not UX enhancements) - Phase 11 already adds interactive controls (step/play/pause), natural place for format toggle ### 2. Pipeline Stage Detail Level **Question:** Show full instruction fields (opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) or just mnemonic? **Recommendation:** Mnemonic only for Phase 10 (`ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`), field breakdown in Phase 11. **Justification:** - Phase 10 requirement (VIZ-01): "Display current instruction in each stage" (not field breakdown) - Phase 11 requirement (VIZ-05): "Instruction display shows current instruction with field breakdown" - Keep Phase 10 focused: Layout + rendering, Phase 11 adds detail ### 3. Pipeline Stage Empty State **Question:** Display `NOP` or `[empty]` for empty stages? **Recommendation:** `NOP` (no operation) to match assembly syntax. **Justification:** - Consistent with assembly language conventions - Educational: NOP is a real instruction (students may encounter in code) - Technical: Bubbles in pipeline effectively NOPs (do nothing, advance clock) ### 4. `; this.stageElements.set(stageName, stageCard); fragment.appendChild(stageCard); }); this.container.appendChild(fragment); } getFullStageName(abbrev) { const names = { IF: 'Instruction Fetch', ID: 'Instruction Decode', EX: 'Execute', MEM: 'Memory Access', WB: 'Write Back' }; return names[abbrev]; } render(state) { state.pipeline.stages.forEach((stageData, index) => { const stageName = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB'][index]; const stageCard = this.stageElements.get(stageName); const instructionEl = stageCard.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); if (stageData.instruction) { const { mnemonic, operands } = stageData.instruction; instructionEl.textContent = `${mnemonic} ${operands.join(', ')}`; stageCard.classList.add('active'); } else { instructionEl.textContent = 'NOP'; stageCard.classList.remove('active'); } }); } } ``` ### 3. ``` - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech finishes - Automatic: Screen readers announce counter updates without manual focus management --- ## Pipeline Visualization (VIZ-01) ### Stage Display **Requirements:** - Show all 5 stages: IF (Instruction Fetch), ID (Instruction Decode), EX (Execute), MEM (Memory), WB (Write Back) - Display current instruction in each stage - Indicate active stages (instruction present vs. empty/bubble) **Implementation approach:** **Stage card structure:** ```html
IF Instruction Fetch
NOP
``` **Color-coded stages (research finding):** Educational CPU visualizers use distinct colors per stage to help students track instruction flow through pipeline. | Stage | Color | Rationale | |-------|-------|-----------| | IF | Green (#4CAF50) | Start of pipeline (green = go) | | ID | Blue (#2196F3) | Decoding/analysis phase | | EX | Orange (#FF9800) | Active computation (warm color = activity) | | MEM | Purple (#9C27B0) | Memory access (distinct from computation) | | WB | Red (#F44336) | Write back (red = completion) | **CSS implementation:** ```css .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="ID"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-id-color); } /* etc. */ ``` **Active stage indicator:** - Add `.active` class when instruction present - Remove when stage holds bubble (NOP/stall) - CSS: Brighter border, slight shadow ### Instruction Display **Format:** Assembly mnemonic + operands (e.g., `ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`) **Empty stage display:** `NOP` (no operation) or `[empty]` (TBD: prefer NOP to match assembly syntax) **CPUState metadata usage:** ```javascript state.pipeline.stages.forEach(stage => { const card = this.container.querySelector(`[data-stage="${stage.name}"]`); const instructionEl = card.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); instructionEl.textContent = stage.instruction?.mnemonic || 'NOP'; card.classList.toggle('active', stage.instruction !== null); }); ``` --- ## Register Visualization (VIZ-02, VIZ-03) ### Register Grid Layout **Requirements:** - Display all 32 registers ($0-$31) - Show current value for each register - Highlight registers that changed in current cycle (VIZ-03) **Grid structure:** ```html
$0 0x00000000
``` **CSS Grid layout:** ```css .register-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } ``` - Responsive: Adjusts columns to viewport width - Consistent sizing: `minmax(120px, 1fr)` ensures readable cells ### Value Display Format **Hex by default:** `0x00000000` (8 hex digits, zero-padded) **Justification:** - Educational standard: Academic CPU simulators use hex (matches memory dumps, opcodes) - Concise: 8 characters vs. 10 for decimal - Deferred toggle: Phase 11+ can add hex/decimal/binary switcher **Register $0 special case:** - Always displays `0x00000000` (hardwired to zero in RISC architectures) - Grayed out styling to indicate read-only ### Change Highlighting (VIZ-03) **CPUState metadata (from Phase 9):** ```javascript state.changedRegisters = [5, 7]; // Registers $5 and $7 changed this cycle ``` **Selective DOM update strategy:** ```javascript // GOOD: Only update changed registers (1-3 per cycle typically) state.changedRegisters.forEach(regIndex => { const cell = this.container.querySelector(`[data-register="${regIndex}"]`); const valueEl = cell.querySelector('.register-value'); valueEl.textContent = formatHex(state.registers[regIndex]); cell.classList.add('changed'); }); // BAD: Full re-render (32 register updates per frame) state.registers.forEach((value, index) => { /* update all */ }); ``` **CSS transition:** ```css .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } ``` - Yellow highlight fades out over 300ms - Remove `.changed` class after transition completes **Performance consideration:** - Non-pipelined simulation (Phase 9): ~1-3 registers change per cycle - Pipelined simulation (Phase 12+): Up to 5 registers per cycle (one per stage) - Selective updates prevent DOM thrashing (3 updates vs. 32) ### Typography **Monospace font (research finding):** Monospace fonts critical for register values (alignment, readability). **Font stack:** ```css .register-value, .instruction-text { font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } ``` **Justification:** - Monaco/Consolas: System monospace fonts (macOS/Windows) - Courier New: Fallback (universal) - No external fonts: Keep performance optimal (no font loading delay) --- ## Execution State (VIZ-06) ### Counter Display **Requirements:** - Display cycle count (increments each animation frame) - Display instruction count (increments when instruction completes WB stage) **Implementation:** ```html

Cycle: 0

Instructions: 0

``` **Update logic:** ```javascript render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } ``` **CPUState fields (from Phase 9):** - `state.cycleCount`: Total cycles elapsed (increments every frame) - `state.instructionCount`: Total instructions completed (increments when instruction exits WB stage) ### Accessibility (aria-live) **Screen reader behavior:** - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech completes - Example: "Cycle: 5, Instructions: 2" (spoken when counters update) **Announcement frequency:** - Non-pipelined (Phase 9): Every cycle (slow pace: 2 FPS base) - Pipelined (Phase 12+): Every cycle (may need throttling if too frequent) **Future enhancement (Phase 11+):** - Add `aria-atomic="true"` to announce full region content (both counters together) - Add `aria-relevant="text"` to only announce text changes (not additions/removals) --- ## Styling Strategy ### CSS Architecture **File structure:** ``` cpu-visualizer/ styles/ visualization.css # Phase 10: Layout, components, colors design-system.css # Existing: Shared tokens (already in codebase) ``` **CSS custom properties (design tokens):** ```css :root { /* Existing tokens from design-system.css */ --color-primary: #2E7D32; /* Forest green */ --color-background: #FFFFFF; --color-text: #212121; /* New tokens for Phase 10 */ --stage-if-color: #4CAF50; /* Green */ --stage-id-color: #2196F3; /* Blue */ --stage-ex-color: #FF9800; /* Orange */ --stage-mem-color: #9C27B0; /* Purple */ --stage-wb-color: #F44336; /* Red */ --color-highlight-yellow: #FFF9C4; /* Register change highlight */ } ``` **Advantages:** - Centralized: All colors defined in one place - Themeable: Future dark mode support (override custom properties) - Consistent: Matches existing design system ### Component-Specific Styles **Pipeline stage cards:** ```css .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); /* Color-coded */ border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; /* Thicker border when active */ } ``` **Register cells:** ```css .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); } .register-cell[data-register="0"] { opacity: 0.6; /* Register $0 always zero, visual cue */ } ``` **Execution counters:** ```css [data-execution-view] p { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0; } [data-execution-view] span { font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; } ``` --- ## Performance Considerations ### Selective DOM Updates **Problem:** Updating all 32 registers every frame causes layout thrashing (browser recalculates styles 32 times). **Solution:** CPUState tracks `changedRegisters` array, only update those elements. **Performance impact:** - Full update: 32 DOM writes + 32 style recalculations per frame - Selective update: 1-3 DOM writes + 1-3 style recalculations per frame - **~10x faster** for typical case (1-3 changed registers) ### Batch DOM Writes **Use DocumentFragment for initial render:** ```javascript const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Register Display Format **Question:** Hex only, or hex + decimal toggle? **Recommendation:** Hex only for Phase 10 (simplicity), defer toggle to Phase 11 (interactive controls). **Justification:** - Hex is educational standard (matches academic tools) - Phase 10 scope: "Basic Visualization" (display works, not UX enhancements) - Phase 11 already adds interactive controls (step/play/pause), natural place for format toggle ### 2. Pipeline Stage Detail Level **Question:** Show full instruction fields (opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) or just mnemonic? **Recommendation:** Mnemonic only for Phase 10 (`ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`), field breakdown in Phase 11. **Justification:** - Phase 10 requirement (VIZ-01): "Display current instruction in each stage" (not field breakdown) - Phase 11 requirement (VIZ-05): "Instruction display shows current instruction with field breakdown" - Keep Phase 10 focused: Layout + rendering, Phase 11 adds detail ### 3. Pipeline Stage Empty State **Question:** Display `NOP` or `[empty]` for empty stages? **Recommendation:** `NOP` (no operation) to match assembly syntax. **Justification:** - Consistent with assembly language conventions - Educational: NOP is a real instruction (students may encounter in code) - Technical: Bubbles in pipeline effectively NOPs (do nothing, advance clock) ### 4. Color Palette Conflict **Question:** Stage colors (green, blue, orange, purple, red) vs. design system primary green (#2E7D32)? **Recommendation:** Use distinct stage colors (from research), keep primary green for UI chrome (header, buttons). **Justification:** - Educational benefit: Color-coded stages help students track instruction flow (established pattern) - Visual hierarchy: Stage colors = content, primary green = navigation/controls - No conflict: Stages use pastel/medium tones (e.g., #4CAF50), primary uses dark tone (#2E7D32) ### 5. Performance Threshold **Question:** How many register updates before performance degrades? **Recommendation:** Measure during implementation (throttle to 3GHz CPU, test with 10+ register changes/frame). **Expected outcome:** - Selective updates (3-5 registers): No performance impact (CSS transitions GPU-accelerated) - Full updates (32 registers): Possible jank at 30+ FPS (forces layout recalculation) - Mitigation: CPUState.changedRegisters prevents full updates by design --- ## Dependencies & Integration ### Phase 9 Outputs (Already Complete) **Required from Phase 9:** 1. **CPUState structure** (cpu-state.js): - `state.pipeline.stages` (array of 5 stages with instruction data) - `state.registers` (Uint32Array of 32 register values) - `state.changedRegisters` (array of register indices that changed) - `state.cycleCount`, `state.instructionCount` 2. **AnimationEngine events** (animation-engine.js): - `cpu:framechange` CustomEvent with `{ state, frameIndex, totalFrames }` payload - Already implemented (09-02-PLAN.md) 3. **Instruction structure** (instruction-set.js): - `instruction.mnemonic` (string, e.g., "ADD") - `instruction.operands` (array, e.g., ["$t0", "$t1", "$t2"]) **Validation:** Existing Phase 9 tests must pass (cpu-state.test.js, animation-engine.test.js). ### Phase 11 Inputs (To Be Consumed) **Outputs from Phase 10:** 1. **Visualization components** (pipeline-view.js, register-view.js, execution-view.js): - Exported classes with `.render(state)` method - Event-driven: Listen to `cpu:framechange`, update DOM 2. **CPUVisualizer coordinator** (cpu-visualizer.js): - Single entry point: `new CPUVisualizer(containerEl)` - Manages child components, delegates rendering 3. **Styling** (visualization.css): - CSS Grid layout (responsive two-column) - Color-coded pipeline stages - Register highlighting transitions **Phase 11 will add:** - Step controls (forward, backward, reset, jump) - Play/pause controls with speed adjustment - Program selector (switch between examples) - Memory visualization (data memory addresses + values) - Instruction detail panel (field breakdown: opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) --- ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Tests **Components to test:** 1. `PipelineView.render(state)` - Stage cards update correctly 2. `RegisterView.render(state)` - Register values update, highlighting works 3. `ExecutionView.render(state)` - Counters increment correctly **Test approach:** - Mock CPUState objects (valid structure, different values) - ${stageName} ${this.getFullStageName(stageName)}
NOP
`; this.stageElements.set(stageName, stageCard); fragment.appendChild(stageCard); }); this.container.appendChild(fragment); } getFullStageName(abbrev) { const names = { IF: 'Instruction Fetch', ID: 'Instruction Decode', EX: 'Execute', MEM: 'Memory Access', WB: 'Write Back' }; return names[abbrev]; } render(state) { state.pipeline.stages.forEach((stageData, index) => { const stageName = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB'][index]; const stageCard = this.stageElements.get(stageName); const instructionEl = stageCard.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); if (stageData.instruction) { const { mnemonic, operands } = stageData.instruction; instructionEl.textContent = `${mnemonic} ${operands.join(', ')}`; stageCard.classList.add('active'); } else { instructionEl.textContent = 'NOP'; stageCard.classList.remove('active'); } }); } } ``` ### 3. for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Color Palette Conflict **Question:** Stage colors (green, blue, orange, purple, red) vs. design system primary green (#2E7D32)? **Recommendation:** Use distinct stage colors (from research), keep primary green for UI chrome (header, buttons). **Justification:** - Educational benefit: Color-coded stages help students track instruction flow (established pattern) - Visual hierarchy: Stage colors = content, primary green = navigation/controls - No conflict: Stages use pastel/medium tones (e.g., #4CAF50), primary uses dark tone (#2E7D32) ### 5. Performance Threshold **Question:** How many register updates before performance degrades? **Recommendation:** Measure during implementation (throttle to 3GHz CPU, test with 10+ register changes/frame). **Expected outcome:** - Selective updates (3-5 registers): No performance impact (CSS transitions GPU-accelerated) - Full updates (32 registers): Possible jank at 30+ FPS (forces layout recalculation) - Mitigation: CPUState.changedRegisters prevents full updates by design --- ## Dependencies & Integration ### Phase 9 Outputs (Already Complete) **Required from Phase 9:** 1. **CPUState structure** (cpu-state.js): - ``` **CSS Grid advantages:** - Responsive: Collapses to single column on narrow viewports - Flexible: Sidebar width adjusts to content, main area fills remaining space - Native: No external layout libraries ### Accessibility **Semantic HTML:** - `

``` - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech finishes - Automatic: Screen readers announce counter updates without manual focus management --- ## Pipeline Visualization (VIZ-01) ### Stage Display **Requirements:** - Show all 5 stages: IF (Instruction Fetch), ID (Instruction Decode), EX (Execute), MEM (Memory), WB (Write Back) - Display current instruction in each stage - Indicate active stages (instruction present vs. empty/bubble) **Implementation approach:** **Stage card structure:** ```html
IF Instruction Fetch
NOP
``` **Color-coded stages (research finding):** Educational CPU visualizers use distinct colors per stage to help students track instruction flow through pipeline. | Stage | Color | Rationale | |-------|-------|-----------| | IF | Green (#4CAF50) | Start of pipeline (green = go) | | ID | Blue (#2196F3) | Decoding/analysis phase | | EX | Orange (#FF9800) | Active computation (warm color = activity) | | MEM | Purple (#9C27B0) | Memory access (distinct from computation) | | WB | Red (#F44336) | Write back (red = completion) | **CSS implementation:** ```css .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="ID"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-id-color); } /* etc. */ ``` **Active stage indicator:** - Add `.active` class when instruction present - Remove when stage holds bubble (NOP/stall) - CSS: Brighter border, slight shadow ### Instruction Display **Format:** Assembly mnemonic + operands (e.g., `ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`) **Empty stage display:** `NOP` (no operation) or `[empty]` (TBD: prefer NOP to match assembly syntax) **CPUState metadata usage:** ```javascript state.pipeline.stages.forEach(stage => { const card = this.container.querySelector(`[data-stage="${stage.name}"]`); const instructionEl = card.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); instructionEl.textContent = stage.instruction?.mnemonic || 'NOP'; card.classList.toggle('active', stage.instruction !== null); }); ``` --- ## Register Visualization (VIZ-02, VIZ-03) ### Register Grid Layout **Requirements:** - Display all 32 registers ($0-$31) - Show current value for each register - Highlight registers that changed in current cycle (VIZ-03) **Grid structure:** ```html
$0 0x00000000
``` **CSS Grid layout:** ```css .register-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: 8px; } ``` - Responsive: Adjusts columns to viewport width - Consistent sizing: `minmax(120px, 1fr)` ensures readable cells ### Value Display Format **Hex by default:** `0x00000000` (8 hex digits, zero-padded) **Justification:** - Educational standard: Academic CPU simulators use hex (matches memory dumps, opcodes) - Concise: 8 characters vs. 10 for decimal - Deferred toggle: Phase 11+ can add hex/decimal/binary switcher **Register $0 special case:** - Always displays `0x00000000` (hardwired to zero in RISC architectures) - Grayed out styling to indicate read-only ### Change Highlighting (VIZ-03) **CPUState metadata (from Phase 9):** ```javascript state.changedRegisters = [5, 7]; // Registers $5 and $7 changed this cycle ``` **Selective DOM update strategy:** ```javascript // GOOD: Only update changed registers (1-3 per cycle typically) state.changedRegisters.forEach(regIndex => { const cell = this.container.querySelector(`[data-register="${regIndex}"]`);
