``` **CSS transition:** ```css .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } ``` - Yellow highlight fades out over 300ms - Remove `.changed` class after transition completes **Performance consideration:** - Non-pipelined simulation (Phase 9): ~1-3 registers change per cycle - Pipelined simulation (Phase 12+): Up to 5 registers per cycle (one per stage) - Selective updates prevent DOM thrashing (3 updates vs. 32) ### Typography **Monospace font (research finding):** Monospace fonts critical for register values (alignment, readability). **Font stack:** ```css .register-value, .instruction-text { font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } ``` **Justification:** - Monaco/Consolas: System monospace fonts (macOS/Windows) - Courier New: Fallback (universal) - No external fonts: Keep performance optimal (no font loading delay) --- ## Execution State (VIZ-06) ### Counter Display **Requirements:** - Display cycle count (increments each animation frame) - Display instruction count (increments when instruction completes WB stage) **Implementation:** ```html

Cycle: 0

Instructions: 0

``` **Update logic:** ```javascript render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } ``` **CPUState fields (from Phase 9):** - `state.cycleCount`: Total cycles elapsed (increments every frame) - `state.instructionCount`: Total instructions completed (increments when instruction exits WB stage) ### Accessibility (aria-live) **Screen reader behavior:** - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech completes - Example: "Cycle: 5, Instructions: 2" (spoken when counters update) **Announcement frequency:** - Non-pipelined (Phase 9): Every cycle (slow pace: 2 FPS base) - Pipelined (Phase 12+): Every cycle (may need throttling if too frequent) **Future enhancement (Phase 11+):** - Add `aria-atomic="true"` to announce full region content (both counters together) - Add `aria-relevant="text"` to only announce text changes (not additions/removals) --- ## Styling Strategy ### CSS Architecture **File structure:** ``` cpu-visualizer/ styles/ visualization.css # Phase 10: Layout, components, colors design-system.css # Existing: Shared tokens (already in codebase) ``` **CSS custom properties (design tokens):** ```css :root { /* Existing tokens from design-system.css */ --color-primary: #2E7D32; /* Forest green */ --color-background: #FFFFFF; --color-text: #212121; /* New tokens for Phase 10 */ --stage-if-color: #4CAF50; /* Green */ --stage-id-color: #2196F3; /* Blue */ --stage-ex-color: #FF9800; /* Orange */ --stage-mem-color: #9C27B0; /* Purple */ --stage-wb-color: #F44336; /* Red */ --color-highlight-yellow: #FFF9C4; /* Register change highlight */ } ``` **Advantages:** - Centralized: All colors defined in one place - Themeable: Future dark mode support (override custom properties) - Consistent: Matches existing design system ### Component-Specific Styles **Pipeline stage cards:** ```css .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); /* Color-coded */ border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; /* Thicker border when active */ } ``` **Register cells:** ```css .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); } .register-cell[data-register="0"] { opacity: 0.6; /* Register $0 always zero, visual cue */ } ``` **Execution counters:** ```css [data-execution-view] p { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0; } [data-execution-view] span { font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; } ``` --- ## Performance Considerations ### Selective DOM Updates **Problem:** Updating all 32 registers every frame causes layout thrashing (browser recalculates styles 32 times). **Solution:** CPUState tracks `changedRegisters` array, only update those elements. **Performance impact:** - Full update: 32 DOM writes + 32 style recalculations per frame - Selective update: 1-3 DOM writes + 1-3 style recalculations per frame - **~10x faster** for typical case (1-3 changed registers) ### Batch DOM Writes **Use DocumentFragment for initial render:** ```javascript const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Register Display Format **Question:** Hex only, or hex + decimal toggle? **Recommendation:** Hex only for Phase 10 (simplicity), defer toggle to Phase 11 (interactive controls). **Justification:** - Hex is educational standard (matches academic tools) - Phase 10 scope: "Basic Visualization" (display works, not UX enhancements) - Phase 11 already adds interactive controls (step/play/pause), natural place for format toggle ### 2. Pipeline Stage Detail Level **Question:** Show full instruction fields (opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) or just mnemonic? **Recommendation:** Mnemonic only for Phase 10 (`ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`), field breakdown in Phase 11. **Justification:** - Phase 10 requirement (VIZ-01): "Display current instruction in each stage" (not field breakdown) - Phase 11 requirement (VIZ-05): "Instruction display shows current instruction with field breakdown" - Keep Phase 10 focused: Layout + rendering, Phase 11 adds detail ### 3. Pipeline Stage Empty State **Question:** Display `NOP` or `[empty]` for empty stages? **Recommendation:** `NOP` (no operation) to match assembly syntax. **Justification:** - Consistent with assembly language conventions - Educational: NOP is a real instruction (students may encounter in code) - Technical: Bubbles in pipeline effectively NOPs (do nothing, advance clock) ### 4. Color Palette Conflict **Question:** Stage colors (green, blue, orange, purple, red) vs. design system primary green (#2E7D32)? **Recommendation:** Use distinct stage colors (from research), keep primary green for UI chrome (header, buttons). **Justification:** - Educational benefit: Color-coded stages help students track instruction flow (established pattern) - Visual hierarchy: Stage colors = content, primary green = navigation/controls - No conflict: Stages use pastel/medium tones (e.g., #4CAF50), primary uses dark tone (#2E7D32) ### 5. Performance Threshold **Question:** How many register updates before performance degrades? **Recommendation:** Measure during implementation (throttle to 3GHz CPU, test with 10+ register changes/frame). **Expected outcome:** - Selective updates (3-5 registers): No performance impact (CSS transitions GPU-accelerated) - Full updates (32 registers): Possible jank at 30+ FPS (forces layout recalculation) - Mitigation: CPUState.changedRegisters prevents full updates by design --- ## Dependencies & Integration ### Phase 9 Outputs (Already Complete) **Required from Phase 9:** 1. **CPUState structure** (cpu-state.js): - `state.pipeline.stages` (array of 5 stages with instruction data) - `state.registers` (Uint32Array of 32 register values) - `state.changedRegisters` (array of register indices that changed) - `state.cycleCount`, `state.instructionCount` 2. **AnimationEngine events** (animation-engine.js): - `cpu:framechange` CustomEvent with `{ state, frameIndex, totalFrames }` payload - Already implemented (09-02-PLAN.md) 3. **Instruction structure** (instruction-set.js): - `instruction.mnemonic` (string, e.g., "ADD") - `instruction.operands` (array, e.g., ["$t0", "$t1", "$t2"]) **Validation:** Existing Phase 9 tests must pass (cpu-state.test.js, animation-engine.test.js). ### Phase 11 Inputs (To Be Consumed) **Outputs from Phase 10:** 1. **Visualization components** (pipeline-view.js, register-view.js, execution-view.js): - Exported classes with `.render(state)` method - Event-driven: Listen to `cpu:framechange`, update DOM 2. **CPUVisualizer coordinator** (cpu-visualizer.js): - Single entry point: `new CPUVisualizer(containerEl)` - Manages child components, delegates rendering 3. **Styling** (visualization.css): - CSS Grid layout (responsive two-column) - Color-coded pipeline stages - Register highlighting transitions **Phase 11 will add:** - Step controls (forward, backward, reset, jump) - Play/pause controls with speed adjustment - Program selector (switch between examples) - Memory visualization (data memory addresses + values) - Instruction detail panel (field breakdown: opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) --- ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Tests **Components to test:** 1. `PipelineView.render(state)` - Stage cards update correctly 2. `RegisterView.render(state)` - Register values update, highlighting works 3. `ExecutionView.render(state)` - Counters increment correctly **Test approach:** - Mock CPUState objects (valid structure, different values) - Dispatch synthetic `cpu:framechange` events - Assert DOM contains expected values, classes **Example test:** ```javascript test('RegisterView highlights changed registers', () => { const state = { registers: new Uint32Array(32), changedRegisters: [5, 7] }; state.registers[5] = 0x12345678; state.registers[7] = 0xABCDEF00; const view = new RegisterView(containerEl); view.render(state); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="5"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="7"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="0"]')).not.toHaveClass('changed'); }); ``` ### Integration Tests **Scenario:** AnimationEngine → CPUVisualizer → DOM updates **Test flow:** 1. Initialize AnimationEngine with pre-scripted sequence (from Phase 9) 2. Initialize CPUVisualizer with container element 3. Call `animationEngine.stepForward()` 4. Assert DOM reflects new state (pipeline stages, registers, counters) **Example test:** ```javascript test('Full animation frame updates visualization', async () => { const sequence = await generateBasicInstructionsSequence(); // Phase 9 function const engine = new AnimationEngine(sequence); const visualizer = new CPUVisualizer(containerEl); engine.stepForward(); // Check pipeline updated const ifStage = containerEl.querySelector('[data-stage="IF"]'); expect(ifStage.textContent).toContain('ADD'); // Check counters updated expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-cycle-count]').textContent).toBe('1'); }); ``` ### Manual Testing **Checklist:** - [ ] All 5 pipeline stages visible on page load - [ ] Registers display in grid layout (4-8 columns depending on viewport) - [ ] Cycle/instruction counters start at 0 - [ ] Step forward → pipeline stages update with instructions - [ ] Step forward → changed registers highlight in yellow - [ ] Highlight fades out after ~300ms - [ ] Counters increment correctly (cycle every step, instruction when WB stage completes) - [ ] Screen reader announces counter changes (test with VoiceOver/NVDA) - [ ] Responsive: Layout adapts to narrow viewport (single column) --- ## Code Examples ### 1. CPUVisualizer (Coordinator) ```javascript // cpu-visualizer.js import { PipelineView } from './pipeline-view.js'; import { RegisterView } from './register-view.js'; import { ExecutionView } from './execution-view.js'; export class CPUVisualizer { constructor(container) { this.container = container; // Initialize child components this.pipelineView = new PipelineView( container.querySelector('[data-pipeline-view]') ); this.registerView = new RegisterView( container.querySelector('[data-register-view]') ); this.executionView = new ExecutionView( container.querySelector('[data-execution-view]') ); // Listen to animation events this.handleFrameChange = this.handleFrameChange.bind(this); window.addEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } handleFrameChange(event) { const { state } = event.detail; // Delegate to child components this.pipelineView.render(state); this.registerView.render(state); this.executionView.render(state); } destroy() { window.removeEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } } ``` ### 2. PipelineView (Stage Visualization) ```javascript // pipeline-view.js export class PipelineView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.stageElements = new Map(); this.initializeStages(); } initializeStages() { const stages = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB']; const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); stages.forEach(stageName => { const stageCard = document.createElement('div'); stageCard.className = 'pipeline-stage'; stageCard.dataset.stage = stageName; stageCard.innerHTML = `
${stageName} ${this.getFullStageName(stageName)}
NOP
`; this.stageElements.set(stageName, stageCard); fragment.appendChild(stageCard); }); this.container.appendChild(fragment); } getFullStageName(abbrev) { const names = { IF: 'Instruction Fetch', ID: 'Instruction Decode', EX: 'Execute', MEM: 'Memory Access', WB: 'Write Back' }; return names[abbrev]; } render(state) { state.pipeline.stages.forEach((stageData, index) => { const stageName = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB'][index]; const stageCard = this.stageElements.get(stageName); const instructionEl = stageCard.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); if (stageData.instruction) { const { mnemonic, operands } = stageData.instruction; instructionEl.textContent = `${mnemonic} ${operands.join(', ')}`; stageCard.classList.add('active'); } else { instructionEl.textContent = 'NOP'; stageCard.classList.remove('active'); } }); } } ``` ### 3. RegisterView (Register Visualization) ```javascript // register-view.js export class RegisterView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.registerCells = []; this.initializeRegisters(); } initializeRegisters() { const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = document.createElement('div'); cell.className = 'register-cell'; cell.dataset.register = i; cell.innerHTML = ` $${i} 0x00000000 `; this.registerCells.push(cell); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); } render(state) { // Selective update: Only changed registers state.changedRegisters.forEach(regIndex => { const cell = this.registerCells[regIndex]; const valueEl = cell.querySelector('.register-value'); // Update value valueEl.textContent = this.formatHex(state.registers[regIndex]); // Add highlight class cell.classList.add('changed'); // Remove after transition setTimeout(() => cell.classList.remove('changed'), 300); }); } formatHex(value) { return '0x' + value.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(8, '0'); } } ``` ### 4. ExecutionView (Counter Display) ```javascript // execution-view.js export class ExecutionView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.cycleEl = container.querySelector('[data-cycle-count]'); this.instructionEl = container.querySelector('[data-instruction-count]'); } render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } } ``` ### 5. CSS (visualization.css) ```css /* Layout */ .cpu-visualizer { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 400px; /* Main + sidebar */ gap: 24px; padding: 24px; } @media (max-width: 768px) { .cpu-visualizer { grid-template-columns: 1fr; /* Stack on mobile */ } } /* Pipeline Stages */ .pipeline-stages { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; } .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left-color: var(--stage-if-color); ``` - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech finishes - Automatic: Screen readers announce counter updates without manual focus management --- ## Pipeline Visualization (VIZ-01) ### Stage Display **Requirements:** - Show all 5 stages: IF (Instruction Fetch), ID (Instruction Decode), EX (Execute), MEM (Memory), WB (Write Back) - Display current instruction in each stage - Indicate active stages (instruction present vs. empty/bubble) **Implementation approach:** **Stage card structure:** ```html
IF Instruction Fetch
NOP
``` **Color-coded stages (research finding):** Educational CPU visualizers use distinct colors per stage to help students track instruction flow through pipeline. | Stage | Color | Rationale | |-------|-------|-----------| | IF | Green (#4CAF50) | Start of pipeline (green = go) | | ID | Blue (#2196F3) | Decoding/analysis phase | | EX | Orange (#FF9800) | Active computation (warm color = activity) | | MEM | Purple (#9C27B0) | Memory access (distinct from computation) | | WB | Red (#F44336) | Write back (red = completion) | **CSS implementation:** ```css .pipeline-stage[data-stage="IF"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); } .pipeline-stage[data-stage="ID"] { border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-id-color); } /* etc. */ ``` **Active stage indicator:** - Add `.active` class when instruction present - Remove when stage holds bubble (NOP/stall) - CSS: Brighter border, slight shadow ### Instruction Display **Format:** Assembly mnemonic + operands (e.g., `ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`) **Empty stage display:** `NOP` (no operation) or `[empty]` (TBD: prefer NOP to match assembly syntax) **CPUState metadata usage:** ```javascript state.pipeline.stages.forEach(stage => { const card = this.container.querySelector(`[data-stage="${stage.name}"]`); const instructionEl = card.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); instructionEl.textContent = stage.instruction?.mnemonic || 'NOP'; card.classList.toggle('active', stage.instruction !== null); }); ``` --- ## Register Visualization (VIZ-02, VIZ-03) ### Register Grid Layout **Requirements:** - Display all 32 registers ($0-$31) - Show current value for each register - Highlight registers that changed in current cycle (VIZ-03) **Grid structure:** ```html

``` **Update logic:** ```javascript render(state) { this.cycleEl.textContent = state.cycleCount; this.instructionEl.textContent = state.instructionCount; } ``` **CPUState fields (from Phase 9):** - `state.cycleCount`: Total cycles elapsed (increments every frame) - `state.instructionCount`: Total instructions completed (increments when instruction exits WB stage) ### Accessibility (aria-live) **Screen reader behavior:** - `aria-live="polite"`: Announces changes after current speech completes - Example: "Cycle: 5, Instructions: 2" (spoken when counters update) **Announcement frequency:** - Non-pipelined (Phase 9): Every cycle (slow pace: 2 FPS base) - Pipelined (Phase 12+): Every cycle (may need throttling if too frequent) **Future enhancement (Phase 11+):** - Add `aria-atomic="true"` to announce full region content (both counters together) - Add `aria-relevant="text"` to only announce text changes (not additions/removals) --- ## Styling Strategy ### CSS Architecture **File structure:** ``` cpu-visualizer/ styles/ visualization.css # Phase 10: Layout, components, colors design-system.css # Existing: Shared tokens (already in codebase) ``` **CSS custom properties (design tokens):** ```css :root { /* Existing tokens from design-system.css */ --color-primary: #2E7D32; /* Orange */ --stage-mem-color: #9C27B0; /* Purple */ --stage-wb-color: #F44336; /* Red */ --color-highlight-yellow: #FFF9C4; /* Register change highlight */ } ``` **Advantages:** - Centralized: All colors defined in one place - Themeable: Future dark mode support (override custom properties) - Consistent: Matches existing design system ### Component-Specific Styles **Pipeline stage cards:** ```css .pipeline-stage { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-left: 4px solid var(--stage-if-color); /* Color-coded */ border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px; background: var(--color-background); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .pipeline-stage.active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-left-width: 6px; /* Thicker border when active */ } ``` **Register cells:** ```css .register-cell { border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px; background: var(--color-background); transition: background-color 0.3s ease-out; } .register-cell.changed { background-color: var(--color-highlight-yellow); } .register-cell[data-register="0"] { opacity: 0.6; /* Register $0 always zero, visual cue */ } ``` **Execution counters:** ```css [data-execution-view] p { font-size: 16px; margin: 8px 0; } [data-execution-view] span { font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Consolas', monospace; } ``` --- ## Performance Considerations ### Selective DOM Updates **Problem:** Updating all 32 registers every frame causes layout thrashing (browser recalculates styles 32 times). **Solution:** CPUState tracks `changedRegisters` array, only update those elements. **Performance impact:** - Full update: 32 DOM writes + 32 style recalculations per frame - Selective update: 1-3 DOM writes + 1-3 style recalculations per frame - **~10x faster** for typical case (1-3 changed registers) ### Batch DOM Writes **Use DocumentFragment for initial render:** ```javascript const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. Register Display Format **Question:** Hex only, or hex + decimal toggle? **Recommendation:** Hex only for Phase 10 (simplicity), defer toggle to Phase 11 (interactive controls). **Justification:** - Hex is educational standard (matches academic tools) - Phase 10 scope: "Basic Visualization" (display works, not UX enhancements) - Phase 11 already adds interactive controls (step/play/pause), natural place for format toggle ### 2. Pipeline Stage Detail Level **Question:** Show full instruction fields (opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) or just mnemonic? **Recommendation:** Mnemonic only for Phase 10 (`ADD $t0, $t1, $t2`), field breakdown in Phase 11. **Justification:** - Phase 10 requirement (VIZ-01): "Display current instruction in each stage" (not field breakdown) - Phase 11 requirement (VIZ-05): "Instruction display shows current instruction with field breakdown" - Keep Phase 10 focused: Layout + rendering, Phase 11 adds detail ### 3. Pipeline Stage Empty State **Question:** Display `NOP` or `[empty]` for empty stages? **Recommendation:** `NOP` (no operation) to match assembly syntax. **Justification:** - Consistent with assembly language conventions - Educational: NOP is a real instruction (students may encounter in code) - Technical: Bubbles in pipeline effectively NOPs (do nothing, advance clock) ### 4. Color Palette Conflict **Question:** Stage colors (green, blue, orange, purple, red) vs. design system primary green (#2E7D32)? **Recommendation:** Use distinct stage colors (from research), keep primary green for UI chrome (header, buttons). **Justification:** - Educational benefit: Color-coded stages help students track instruction flow (established pattern) - Visual hierarchy: Stage colors = content, primary green = navigation/controls - No conflict: Stages use pastel/medium tones (e.g., #4CAF50), primary uses dark tone (#2E7D32) ### 5. Performance Threshold **Question:** How many register updates before performance degrades? **Recommendation:** Measure during implementation (throttle to 3GHz CPU, test with 10+ register changes/frame). **Expected outcome:** - Selective updates (3-5 registers): No performance impact (CSS transitions GPU-accelerated) - Full updates (32 registers): Possible jank at 30+ FPS (forces layout recalculation) - Mitigation: CPUState.changedRegisters prevents full updates by design --- ## Dependencies & Integration ### Phase 9 Outputs (Already Complete) **Required from Phase 9:** 1. **CPUState structure** (cpu-state.js): - `state.pipeline.stages` (array of 5 stages with instruction data) - `state.registers` (Uint32Array of 32 register values) - `state.changedRegisters` (array of register indices that changed) - `state.cycleCount`, `state.instructionCount` 2. **AnimationEngine events** (animation-engine.js): - `cpu:framechange` CustomEvent with `{ state, frameIndex, totalFrames }` payload - Already implemented (09-02-PLAN.md) 3. **Instruction structure** (instruction-set.js): - `instruction.mnemonic` (string, e.g., "ADD") - `instruction.operands` (array, e.g., ["$t0", "$t1", "$t2"]) **Validation:** Existing Phase 9 tests must pass (cpu-state.test.js, animation-engine.test.js). ### Phase 11 Inputs (To Be Consumed) **Outputs from Phase 10:** 1. **Visualization components** (pipeline-view.js, register-view.js, execution-view.js): - Exported classes with `.render(state)` method - Event-driven: Listen to `cpu:framechange`, update DOM 2. **CPUVisualizer coordinator** (cpu-visualizer.js): - Single entry point: `new CPUVisualizer(containerEl)` - Manages child components, delegates rendering 3. **Styling** (visualization.css): - CSS Grid layout (responsive two-column) - Color-coded pipeline stages - Register highlighting transitions **Phase 11 will add:** - Step controls (forward, backward, reset, jump) - Play/pause controls with speed adjustment - Program selector (switch between examples) - Memory visualization (data memory addresses + values) - Instruction detail panel (field breakdown: opcode, rs, rt, rd, immediate) --- ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Tests **Components to test:** 1. `PipelineView.render(state)` - Stage cards update correctly 2. `RegisterView.render(state)` - Register values update, highlighting works 3. `ExecutionView.render(state)` - Counters increment correctly **Test approach:** - Mock CPUState objects (valid structure, different values) - Dispatch synthetic `cpu:framechange` events - Assert DOM contains expected values, classes **Example test:** ```javascript test('RegisterView highlights changed registers', () => { const state = { registers: new Uint32Array(32), changedRegisters: [5, 7] }; state.registers[5] = 0x12345678; state.registers[7] = 0xABCDEF00; const view = new RegisterView(containerEl); view.render(state); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="5"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="7"]')).toHaveClass('changed'); expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-register="0"]')).not.toHaveClass('changed'); }); ``` ### Integration Tests **Scenario:** AnimationEngine → CPUVisualizer → DOM updates **Test flow:** 1. Initialize AnimationEngine with pre-scripted sequence (from Phase 9) 2. Initialize CPUVisualizer with container element 3. Call `animationEngine.stepForward()` 4. Assert DOM reflects new state (pipeline stages, registers, counters) **Example test:** ```javascript test('Full animation frame updates visualization', async () => { const sequence = await generateBasicInstructionsSequence(); // Phase 9 function const engine = new AnimationEngine(sequence); const visualizer = new CPUVisualizer(containerEl); engine.stepForward(); // Check pipeline updated const ifStage = containerEl.querySelector('[data-stage="IF"]'); expect(ifStage.textContent).toContain('ADD'); // Check counters updated expect(containerEl.querySelector('[data-cycle-count]').textContent).toBe('1'); }); ``` ### Manual Testing **Checklist:** - [ ] All 5 pipeline stages visible on page load - [ ] Registers display in grid layout (4-8 columns depending on viewport) - [ ] Cycle/instruction counters start at 0 - [ ] Step forward → pipeline stages update with instructions - [ ] Step forward → changed registers highlight in yellow - [ ] Highlight fades out after ~300ms - [ ] Counters increment correctly (cycle every step, instruction when WB stage completes) - [ ] Screen reader announces counter changes (test with VoiceOver/NVDA) - [ ] Responsive: Layout adapts to narrow viewport (single column) --- ## Code Examples ### 1. CPUVisualizer (Coordinator) ```javascript // cpu-visualizer.js import { PipelineView } from './pipeline-view.js'; import { RegisterView } from './register-view.js'; import { ExecutionView } from './execution-view.js'; export class CPUVisualizer { constructor(container) { this.container = container; // Initialize child components this.pipelineView = new PipelineView( container.querySelector('[data-pipeline-view]') ); this.registerView = new RegisterView( container.querySelector('[data-register-view]') ); this.executionView = new ExecutionView( container.querySelector('[data-execution-view]') ); // Listen to animation events this.handleFrameChange = this.handleFrameChange.bind(this); window.addEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } handleFrameChange(event) { const { state } = event.detail; // Delegate to child components this.pipelineView.render(state); this.registerView.render(state); this.executionView.render(state); } destroy() { window.removeEventListener('cpu:framechange', this.handleFrameChange); } } ``` ### 2. PipelineView (Stage Visualization) ```javascript // pipeline-view.js export class PipelineView { constructor(container) { this.container = container; this.stageElements = new Map(); this.initializeStages(); } initializeStages() { const stages = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB']; const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment(); stages.forEach(stageName => { const stageCard = document.createElement('div'); stageCard.className = 'pipeline-stage'; stageCard.dataset.stage = stageName; stageCard.innerHTML = `
${stageName} ${this.getFullStageName(stageName)}
NOP

for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) { const cell = this.createRegisterCell(i); fragment.appendChild(cell); } this.container.appendChild(fragment); // Single DOM insertion ``` **Advantages:** - Single reflow: Browser calculates layout once (not 32 times) - ~5x faster initial render (measured in DOM benchmarks) ### CSS Transitions vs. JavaScript Animations **Use CSS transitions for highlighting:** - GPU-accelerated: Smooth 60 FPS animations - Declarative: Less JavaScript code, easier to maintain - Automatic cleanup: `.changed` class removed after transition completes **Avoid JavaScript animations:** - `setInterval`/`setTimeout`: Not frame-aligned, jank risk - Manual style changes: Forces synchronous layout recalculation --- ## Open Questions & Recommendations ### 1. `; this.stageElements.set(stageName, stageCard); fragment.appendChild(stageCard); }); this.container.appendChild(fragment); } getFullStageName(abbrev) { const names = { IF: 'Instruction Fetch', ID: 'Instruction Decode', EX: 'Execute', MEM: 'Memory Access', WB: 'Write Back' }; return names[abbrev]; } render(state) { state.pipeline.stages.forEach((stageData, index) => { const stageName = ['IF', 'ID', 'EX', 'MEM', 'WB'][index]; const stageCard = this.stageElements.get(stageName); const instructionEl = stageCard.querySelector('[data-stage-instruction]'); if (stageData.instruction) { const { mnemonic, operands } = stageData.instruction; instructionEl.textContent = `${mnemonic} ${operands.join(', ')}`; stageCard.classList.add('active'); } else { instructionEl.textContent = 'NOP'; stageCard.classList.remove('active'); } }); } } ``` ### 3. 1→/*
     2→ * Design System - Single Source of Truth for Visual Tokens
     3→ *
     4→ * This file defines all design tokens (colors, spacing, typography, animation)
     5→ * as CSS custom properties. All pages in the portfolio link to this file.
     6→ *
     7→ * Usage: var(--color-primary), var(--space-md), var(--text-lg), etc.
     8→ */
     9→
    10→:root {
    11→  /* ============================================
    12→   * COLOR PALETTE - Unified Green Theme
    13→   * ============================================ */
    14→
    15→  /* Primary Colors (Forest Green) */
    16→  --color-primary: #2E7D32;           /* Forest green - AA contrast 4.98:1 on white */
    17→  --color-primary-dark: #1B5E20;      /* Dark forest green - AA contrast 8.59:1 on white */
    18→
    19→  /* Accent Colors (Light Green) */
    20→  --color-accent: #4CAF50;            /* Light green - for dark backgrounds only */
    21→  --color-accent-light: #81C784;      /* Pastel green - borders/subtle highlights */
    22→
    23→  /* Surface Colors */
    24→  --color-surface: #ffffff;           /* Primary background */
    25→  --color-surface-alt: #f8f9fa;       /* Secondary background */
    26→  --color-surface-dim: #f5f5f5;       /* Tertiary background */
    27→
    28→  /* Text Colors */
    29→  --color-text: #333333;              /* Body text */
    30→  --color-text-heading: #2c3e50;      /* Headings */
    31→  --color-text-muted: #666666;        /* Secondary text */
    32→  --color-text-light: #555555;        /* Tertiary text */
    33→
    34→  /* Border Colors */
    35→  --color-border: #e0e0e0;            /* Primary borders */
    36→  --color-border-light: #dddddd;      /* Light borders */
    37→
    38→  /* Special Purpose Colors */
    39→  --color-code-bg: #1e1e1e;           /* Code block background */
    40→  --color-footer-bg: #2c3e50;         /* Footer background */
    41→
    42→  /* ============================================
    43→   * GRADIENTS
    44→   * ============================================ */
    45→
    46→  --gradient-primary: linear-gradient(135deg, #2E7D32 0%, #1B5E20 100%);
    47→  --gradient-header: linear-gradient(135deg, #2c3e50 0%, #34495e 100%);
    48→
    49→  /* ============================================
    50→   * SPACING - Fibonacci-Based Rem Scale
    51→   * ============================================ */
    52→
    53→  --space-xs: 0.5rem;     /* 8px - Minimal spacing */
    54→  --space-sm: 0.75rem;    /* 12px - Tight spacing */
    55→  --space-md: 1.25rem;    /* 20px - Standard spacing */
    56→  --space-lg: 2rem;       /* 32px - Large spacing */
    57→  --space-xl: 3.25rem;    /* 52px - Extra large spacing */
    58→
    59→  /* ============================================
    60→   * TYPOGRAPHY
    61→   * ============================================ */
    62→
    63→  /* Font Families */
    64→  --font-body: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, sans-serif;
    65→  --font-mono: 'Monaco', 'Menlo', 'Ubuntu Mono', 'Consolas', monospace;
    66→
    67→  /* Font Sizes (Fluid Typography with clamp) */
    68→  --text-xs: clamp(0.75rem, 0.7rem + 0.25vw, 0.875rem);      /* 12px - 14px */
    69→  --text-sm: clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.4vw, 1rem);          /* 14px - 16px */
    70→  --text-base: clamp(1rem, 0.95rem + 0.25vw, 1.125rem);      /* 16px - 18px */
    71→  --text-lg: clamp(1.125rem, 1rem + 0.6vw, 1.5rem);          /* 18px - 24px */
    72→  --text-xl: clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.5vw, 2.5rem);          /* 24px - 40px */
    73→
    74→  /* Line Heights */
    75→  --leading-body: 1.6;        /* Body text readability */
    76→  --leading-heading: 1.2;     /* Tight heading spacing */
    77→  --leading-code: 1.4;        /* Code block readability */
    78→
    79→  /* ============================================
    80→   * ANIMATION TIMING
    81→   * ============================================ */
    82→
    83→  /* Duration */
    84→  --timing-instant: 150ms;    /* Instant feedback (hover, focus) */
    85→  --timing-standard: 250ms;   /* Standard transitions */
    86→  --timing-complex: 350ms;    /* Complex animations */
    87→
    88→  /* Easing Functions */
    89→  --easing-standard: ease;    /* General purpose */
    90→  --easing-enter: ease-out;   /* Entering elements */
    91→  --easing-exit: ease-in;     /* Exiting elements */
    92→}
    93→
    94→/* ============================================
    95→ * ACCESSIBILITY - Respect User Preferences
    96→ * ============================================ */
    97→
    98→@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    99→  *,
   100→  *::before,
   101→  *::after {
   102→    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
   103→    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
   104→    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
   105→  }
   106→}
   107→
   108→/* ========================================
   109→   INTERACTIVE STATES
   110→   ======================================== */
   111→
   112→/* Standard button/link hover transition */
   113→a, button, [role="tab"], .btn, .project-card, .repo-item {
   114→  transition: background var(--timing-instant) var(--easing-standard),
   115→              color var(--timing-instant) var(--easing-standard),
   116→              transform var(--timing-instant) var(--easing-standard),
   117→              box-shadow var(--timing-standard) var(--easing-standard),
   118→              border-color var(--timing-instant) var(--easing-standard);
   119→}
   120→
   121→/* Focus-visible for keyboard users only (not mouse clicks) */
   122→a:focus-visible,
   123→button:focus-visible,
   124→[role="tab"]:focus-visible,
   125→input:focus-visible,
   126→select:focus-visible {
   127→  outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
   128→  outline-offset: 2px;
   129→}
   130→
   131→/* Subtle press effect for buttons */
   132→button:active:not(:disabled),
   133→.btn:active {
   134→  transform: scale(0.98);
   135→}
   136→
   137→/* ========================================
   138→   TYPOGRAPHY BASE
   139→   ======================================== */
   140→
   141→body {
   142→  font-family: var(--font-body);
   143→  font-size: var(--text-base);
   144→  line-height: var(--leading-body);
   145→}
   146→
   147→h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6 {
   148→  line-height: var(--leading-heading);
   149→}
   150→
   151→code, pre, .code-snippet {
   152→  font-family: var(--font-mono);
   153→  line-height: var(--leading-code);
   154→}
   155→
   156→/* Smooth scroll for anchor links */
   157→html {
   158→  scroll-behavior: smooth;
   159→}

# Phase 10 Plan 01: Basic Visualization Components

**One-liner:** Pure render components (PipelineView, RegisterView, ExecutionView) with CSS Grid layout, stage-specific colors, selective register updates, and assembly-style instruction formatting

## What Was Built

Created the three leaf visualization view components and their shared CSS stylesheet:

1. **visualization.css (180 lines)**
   - Stage color tokens (IF=green, ID=blue, EX=orange, MEM=purple, WB=red)
   - CSS Grid layout with 2-column desktop, 1-column mobile (768px breakpoint)
   - Pipeline stage cards with color-coded left borders (4px normal, 6px active)
   - Register grid with auto-fill minmax(130px, 1fr) responsive columns
   - Register change highlighting (yellow background, 300ms fade-out)
   - Register $0 reduced opacity (hardwired-to-zero visual cue)
   - Execution counter styling with monospace fonts
   - Extends design-system.css without duplicating existing tokens

2. **pipeline-view.js (154 lines)**
   - Renders 5 stage cards (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with data-stage attributes
   - Displays instruction mnemonic + formatted operands for active stages
   - Shows 'NOP' for inactive stages
   - Assembly-style operand formatting:
     - R-type (ADD/SUB): `$rd, $rs, $rt` → `$10, $8, $9`
     - I-type (ADDI): `$rt, $rs, imm` → `$8, $0, 10`
     - I-type (LW): `$rt, imm($rs)` → `$12, 0($8)`
     - S-type (SW): `$rt, imm($rs)` → `$10, 0($8)`
     - B-type (BEQ): `$rs, $rt, offset` → `$8, $8, 2`
     - J-type (J): `target` → `0`
   - DocumentFragment for batch DOM construction
   - Map<stageName, element> for O(1) stage lookups

3. **register-view.js (103 lines)**
   - 32-register grid with $0-$31 labels
   - Selective update: only renders changed registers (from state.changedRegisters Set)
   - Removes 'changed' class from previous frame's highlights before applying new ones
   - Hex formatting: `0x` prefix, uppercase, 8-digit zero-padded
   - First render: updates all 32 registers (initialization)
   - Subsequent renders: updates only 1-3 registers per frame (typical)
   - Defensive handling: Register $0 always shows 0x00000000 even if in changedRegisters

4. **execution-view.js (66 lines)**
   - Displays cycleCount and instructionCount from CPUState
   - Queries existing data-cycle-count/data-instruction-count spans
   - Creates structure if container is empty
   - Simple textContent updates per frame
   - Container expects aria-live="polite" (set by parent CPUVisualizer in Plan 02)

## Implementation Notes

**IIFE Module Pattern:**
All JS files follow Phase 9 pattern: IIFE wrapper with `window.PipelineView` export. No ES6 modules for consistency with existing codebase.

**Performance Optimizations:**
- DocumentFragment: Single DOM insertion for all 32 registers (not 32 separate appends)
- Selective updates: RegisterView only touches changed registers (1-3 per frame, not all 32)
- Map lookups: PipelineView uses Map for O(1) stage element access
- CSS transitions: Hardware-accelerated background-color animation (not JavaScript)

**Instruction Display Logic:**
In non-pipelined mode (Phase 9), only one stage is active per frame. The instruction object is stored in `state.pipeline.IF.instruction` and flows through all 5 stages. PipelineView reads from IF stage for all active stages, avoiding instruction duplication in state.

**Register $0 Handling:**
- CSS: `[data-register="0"]` has `opacity: 0.6` to indicate special status
- JS: Defensive check ensures $0 always displays 0x00000000
- State: CPUState.setRegister() already prevents writes to $0, but view layer is defensive

**Accessibility:**
- ExecutionView container expects `aria-live="polite"` for screen reader announcements
- Pipeline stages use semantic HTML with clear labels
- Register labels use `$N` convention matching MIPS/RISC-V documentation
- CSS respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (inherited from design-system.css)

## Deviations from Plan

None - plan executed exactly as written.

## Testing Notes

These are pure render components with no internal state beyond DOM references. Testing in Plan 02:

1. **Integration test with CPUState:** Create mock state, call render(), verify DOM
2. **Register highlighting:** Trigger changedRegisters, verify 'changed' class applied/removed
3. **Pipeline stages:** Set active=true for each stage, verify 'active' class and instruction text
4. **Instruction formatting:** Test all 8 instruction types (ADD, SUB, ADDI, LW, SW, BEQ, J, NOP)
5. **Responsive layout:** Resize viewport, verify 2-column → 1-column at 768px
6. **Register $0 opacity:** Verify reduced opacity in computed styles

```css
--stage-if-color: #4CAF50;   /* Green */

```

```javascript
// Selective register update (register-view.js:68-82)
const changed = Array.from(state.changedRegisters || []);
changed.forEach(index => {
  const cell = this.registerCells[index];
  const valueEl = cell.querySelector('.register-value');
  const value = index === 0 ? 0 : state.registers[index];
  valueEl.textContent = '0x' + value.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(8, '0');
  cell.classList.add('changed');
});
```

```javascript
// Instruction formatting (pipeline-view.js:98-108)
switch (type) {
  case 'R':
    return `$${rd}, $${rs}, $${rt}`;  // ADD $10, $8, $9
  case 'I':
    if (instruction.mnemonic === 'ADDI') {
      return `$${rt}, $${rs}, ${immediate}`;  // ADDI $8, $0, 10
    } else if (instruction.mnemonic === 'LW') {
      return `$${rt}, ${immediate}($${rs})`;  // LW $12, 0($8)
    }
    break;
  // ...
}
```
